key_insight: Jointly training separate planning and execution agents improves long-horizon web task success over a larger monolithic agent in the reported evaluation.
engineering_relevance: Role-specialized smaller models offer a promising alternative to scaling a single model for complex GUI automation.
method: Separate task decomposition from subtask-conditioned action execution.
Fine-tune both agents using teacher-generated subtask annotations from multimodal GUI trajectories.
Jointly optimize both agents with hierarchical rollout grouping and role-specific GRPO advantages.
evidence_signal: On WebArena-Lite-v2, the 7B decomposer plus 7B actor achieved 37.2% average success versus 24% for an RL-fine-tuned ScaleCUA-32B under the same protocol; ablations favored joint updates over actor-only updates.
watch_item: Generalization beyond WebArena-Lite-v2 and the inference cost of coordinating two agents remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
